name: user-rules
description: User-scope CC Safety Net rules. Deployed to ~/.cc-safety-net/rules/user-rules/rulebook.json.
author: vendor-omo

rules.name: block-git-commit-am
rules.reason: git commit -am stages ALL tracked modifications indiscriminately. Use git add <file> then git commit -m instead.

rules.name: block-git-rebase-continue
rules.reason: git rebase --continue/--skip/--abort should be run intentionally by the user. Auto-continuing rebases can commit unintended changes.

rules.name: block-bd-notes-flag
rules.reason: Use --append-notes instead to preserve existing notes and maintain audit trail.

rules.name: block-stop-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct container stop is blocked to protect service availability. Use orchestrated workflows or the API to manage service termination.

rules.name: block-kill-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct container kill is blocked. Abrupt termination causes data corruption in LiteLLM/Postgres. Use the API for graceful shutdown.

rules.name: block-rm-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct container removal is blocked. Re-deploying manually bypasses the infrastructure-as-code state. Use Nomad/Ansible for removal.

rules.name: block-restart-docker-entirely
rules.reason: NEVER restart containers directly. This bypasses service orchestration (Nomad/Consul) and can lead to inconsistent state or data loss. Use the API or Nomad to manage service lifecycle.

rules.name: block-exec-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct exec into containers is blocked for security and integrity. Container states must be managed via configuration, not manual shell access. Use the API for troubleshooting.

rules.name: block-update-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct resource updates are blocked. Use Nomad job specs to adjust CPU/Memory limits.

rules.name: block-rename-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Container renaming is blocked to prevent breaking service discovery and monitoring tools.

rules.name: block-volume-rm-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Direct volume removal is strictly blocked to prevent permanent data loss. Volumes must be managed via Nomad/Ansible job specs.

rules.name: block-volume-create-docker-entirely
rules.reason: Manual volume creation is blocked to maintain infrastructure-as-code consistency. Define volumes in mise tasks or Nomad jobs.

rules.name: block-compose-down-litellm-services
rules.reason: NEVER bring down litellm/litellm-local/omniroute via docker compose down. Removes containers, networks, and potentially volumes. Use the API to manage services instead.

rules.name: block-compose-rm-litellm-services
rules.reason: NEVER remove litellm/litellm-local/omniroute containers via docker compose rm. Use the API to manage services instead.

rules.name: block-compose-stop-litellm-services
rules.reason: NEVER stop litellm/litellm-local/omniroute via docker compose. Use the API to manage them instead.

rules.name: block-git-stash-mutations
rules.reason: Do not mutate stashes in shared work. Others may be working in this directory. Read-only stash operations (list, show, branch, log) are allowed. If action is truly needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-reset-hard
rules.reason: Hard reset discards local work and can remove others' changes. Use safer targeted operations. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-reset-mixed
rules.reason: Mixed reset rewrites index state and can disrupt shared dirty work. Use explicit file-level actions. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-reset-merge
rules.reason: Reset modes can unexpectedly alter local changes in shared directories. Prefer explicit safe steps. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-clean-force
rules.reason: git clean can permanently remove untracked files from collaborators. Use targeted cleanup only. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-checkout-discard
rules.reason: checkout -- discards local file changes and may delete others' edits. Use explicit review-first workflows. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-restore-worktree
rules.reason: git restore can discard tracked modifications in shared worktrees. Prefer explicit file-safe steps. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-add-all
rules.reason: git add -A / -a stages ALL changed files indiscriminately. Always use 'git add <specific-file>' or 'git add <directory>/' to stage intentionally. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-add-dot
rules.reason: git add . stages ALL files in the current directory recursively. Always use 'git add <specific-file>' or 'git add <directory>/' to stage intentionally. If needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-commit-no-verify
rules.reason: ALWAYS run pre-commit hooks. Bypassing hooks risks committing broken or unvalidated code. If action is truly needed, provide a single-line command humans can copy and run as-is.

rules.name: block-git-checkout-branch-reset
rules.reason: git checkout -B force-resets branch refs and can temporarily orphan large local histories. Use explicit merge workflows instead.

rules.name: block-git-switch-force-create
rules.reason: git switch -C force-resets branch refs and can rewrite the current branch unexpectedly. Use explicit safe branch operations instead.

rules.name: block-git-branch-force-move
rules.reason: Forced branch moves or renames can rewrite refs and hide work unexpectedly. Use review-first branch operations instead.

rules.name: block-git-rebase-entirely
rules.reason: Rebase rewrites commit history and is blocked in this environment. Merge instead of rebasing shared or valuable branch histories.

rules.name: allow-rm-bd-sub-skills
rules.reason: Allow deleting deprecated bd sub-skill directories. User explicitly requested consolidation.

rules.name: allow-rm-beads-subdirs
rules.reason: Allow removing symlink subdirs in beads/ skill. User explicitly requested beads as standalone.

rules.name: block-gcloud-destructive-verbs
rules.reason: Mutation-capable gcloud operations are blocked by default to protect cloud resources, especially Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, and other serverless services.

rules.name: block-bq-destructive-verbs
rules.reason: BigQuery mutation commands are blocked by default to protect datasets, tables, jobs, and IAM configuration.

rules.name: block-gh-repo-delete-or-archive
rules.reason: Destructive GitHub repository lifecycle actions are blocked by default.

rules.name: block-gh-public-repo-create
rules.reason: Public GitHub repository creation is blocked by default. Create repos as private/internal only unless explicitly approved by a human.

rules.name: block-gh-visibility-change
rules.reason: GitHub repository visibility changes are blocked by default to prevent accidental public exposure.

rules.name: block-glab-repo-delete-or-archive
rules.reason: Destructive GitLab repository lifecycle actions are blocked by default.

rules.name: block-glab-public-repo-create
rules.reason: Public GitLab repository creation is blocked by default. Create repos as private/internal only unless explicitly approved by a human.

rules.name: block-tmux-kill-server
rules.reason: Killing the tmux/wezterm server destroys ALL sessions, panes, and in-flight work across every client. Do NOT run this automatically — hand the exact command back to the user and let them run it themselves.

rules.name: block-tmux-kill-session
rules.reason: Killing the tmux/wezterm server destroys ALL sessions, panes, and in-flight work across every client. Do NOT run this automatically — hand the exact command back to the user and let them run it themselves.

rules.name: block-pkill-tmux-wezterm
rules.reason: Killing the tmux/wezterm server destroys ALL sessions, panes, and in-flight work across every client. Do NOT run this automatically — hand the exact command back to the user and let them run it themselves.

rules.name: block-killall-tmux-wezterm
rules.reason: Killing the tmux/wezterm server destroys ALL sessions, panes, and in-flight work across every client. Do NOT run this automatically — hand the exact command back to the user and let them run it themselves.
